evidence.quote: many-body physics I’m an Assistant Professor of Computer Science and Physics at EPFL. As a theorist, I work at the intersection of quantum algorithms, coding theory, learning theory and many-body physics . I often end up using tools from coding/learning theory in order to derive fundamental limits and design algorithms for quantum tasks: from Gibbs-state preparation and optimization, to cryptography and limitations of error mitigation . I also use computational complexity as a lens on physics — thermalization, chaos , and randomness — asking what is classically simulable and what is (not) observable experimentally.
